purpose: Companion scenario data for the bundled sample Microsoft Project file. Documents the Consequence of Delay (JEV) integration's actual INPUT CONTRACT for tasks in this sample, plus a clear, honest basis for what the assessment would be judged on.
important: No JEV API call is made while running the sample offline.
No values in this file are presented as live JEV responses.
Consequence of Delay (CD) in offline mode is provisional (0.5) and flagged for review.
With a configured TYPESAFE_API_KEY the app sends task_name + task_notes to the real JEV integration; these are the exact fields documented below.
Manual assessment levels below are demonstrations, not API calls.

input_contract.scale: 0..3, divided by 3 to become the CD share of the priority index
input_contract.instructions: What is the worst NON-SCHEDULE business consequence (cost, safety, quality, contract, production) if this activity finishes late? Judge only the business impact of the delay itself.
levels: Level 0 - Only the activity itself is delayed; there is no material downstream non-schedule business consequence.
Level 1 - The delay causes a small, recoverable consequence, such as limited added cost or rework.
Level 2 - The delay causes a significant consequence involving cost, quality risk, or a customer/supplier commitment.
Level 3 - The delay can cause a major consequence: production stoppage, a safety/regulatory violation, a contractual penalty, or the loss of a non-movable production/window/resource opportunity.

scenarios.task_notes: A late delivery of the press blocks every mechanical installation task downstream and jeopardizes the production start date.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: Press delivery is the single gate that every mechanical installation task waits on; the production start date is contractually anchored. Crosses into 'production stoppage' territory if it slips.

scenarios.task_notes: Late motor connections stall every downstream integration task; production start slips.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: Significant consequence (widespread downstream stall) but still recoverable by extending the shift and re-sequencing; not an automatic production stoppage.

scenarios.task_notes: Missing safety approval blocks the energization and integration phases; regulatory and safety consequences are material.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: Safety sign-off is regulatory and non-movable; a slip here is explicitly a safety/regulatory violation exposure and directly blocks the energization phase.

scenarios.task_notes: Delays here stall the integration phase and the production start; commercial impact of late automation is high.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: Strong commercial impact and a widespread downstream stall, but not an immediate safety or contractual-penalty case.

scenarios.task_notes: A late trial run pushes back the production start; customer commitments assume this window.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: Customer commitments depend on this window; a slip risks contractual exposure but typically does not halt an already-running production line.

scenarios.task_notes: Vendor supplier delay flagged; re-plan if factory acceptance slips — production start depends on it.
scenarios.assessment_rationale: The press build monitoring is the early-warning task for the delivery scenario; recoverable with a change of shipping mode or factory acceptance reprioritization.
Final lighting has no downstream non-schedule business consequence; included as a baseline-level example against the high-consequence scenarios.
